title: Last commands leave bin/relay, the tables go
what: Move the last commands out of bin/relay and delete the tables.

- Modules: status, report, calibrate, profile, flows, rules, candidate as lib/relay_cmd/<name>.py; improve, bench and license as packages (lib/relay_cmd/improve/, bench/, license/) with one module per action (improve: log, suggest, adopt and the others in `cmd_improve`; bench: list, run and the others in `cmd_bench`; license: add, check and the others in `cmd_license`), each with USAGE, WRITES and run, and an `__init__.py` header with USAGE and WRITES for the bare use. Find the functions by name in bin/relay (cmd_status, cmd_report, cmd_calibrate, cmd_improve, cmd_bench, cmd_candidate, cmd_profile, cmd_flows, cmd_rules, cmd_license).

- Delete from bin/relay: the `COMMANDS` table, the docstring blocks of every command, and the imports only the moved code used. bin/relay ends as the header, the path setup and `main` calling lib/relay_cli.py: about 15 lines.

- Delete the guard's table (plugins/delegate/hooks/read-only-guard.py) and the table half of tests/relay_commands.py (`names()` then reads the module walk only; `load_relay`'s COMMANDS read goes). The guard then decides only from modules (resolution order 1, 3, 4). The frozen verdicts and the agreement test of move 5 must pass unchanged before the table goes: keep the table until they do, then delete it. The frozen verdicts stay in the test file as literals.

- New `ast` test (tests/test_cmd_ast_bin_relay.py or inside an existing file): no string literal in bin/relay equals the name of a module under lib/relay_cmd, which fails on a `{"queue": ...}` table or an `argv[1] == "queue"`.

- Tests: per-command files per the convention. Move 3 as built: under the empty RELAY_ROOT, calibrate, flows and rules fail on a missing file before they read their arguments (tests/test_cmd_smoke.py has "[Errno 2]" cases for them), so their own files must hold a smoke case whose outcome depends on an argument; status ("No ledger events in the last 12 hours"), report ("No sessions found in that period"), profile (`profile nosuch` exit 1, "no profile 'nosuch'"), candidate (exit 2, "relay candidate <name>"), improve (`improve log`, "No adoptions yet."), bench (exit 2, "relay bench <profileA>") and license (exit 2, "relay license add") have working cases there. tests/test_help_is_safe.py's FLOOR check (the 21 names) must stay satisfied by the module walk alone.
Done: full gate green; all 21 commands behave as before; bin/relay is about 15 lines; the guard has no table; the ast test fails on a restored table.

Module interface (every moved command): `USAGE: str` whose first line is `relay <cmd> ...`; `WRITES: bool`; optional `READ_FLAGS` (sync's `--dry`); `def run(args: list[str]) -> int`. Names match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, a typed `-` maps to `_`. A package's `__init__.py` has the header `USAGE`, `WRITES` for its bare use, and an optional `fallback(args)`; mixed commands (queue, check, improve, bench, license) become packages with one module per action.

Test convention (tests/cmd_harness.py docstring, move 3): each command's own test file tests/test_cmd_<cmd>.py (tests/test_cmd_<cmd>_<action>.py for an action of a package) holds two cases: (1) `relay <cmd> --help` prints the usage lines it printed before the move, copied as a literal; (2) one smoke case with harmless arguments asserting the exit code and one output line, run through `run_relay` from tests/cmd_harness.py (it returns code, stdout, stderr and the files written, in temporary HOME, RELAY_HOME, RELAY_ROOT and cwd). For a command that cannot run in a temporary tree, the case is its usage refusal. tests/test_cmd_files.py fails, naming the file, for any module under lib/relay_cmd/ without its test file. tests/test_cmd_smoke.py already holds one table SMOKE with a case per command (all 21); keep the moved command's case there working, and note that under the empty RELAY_ROOT calibrate, install, flows, rules and doctor fail on a missing file before they read their arguments, so for those the command's own file must replace the case with one whose outcome depends on an argument. This catches an off-by-one in how the dispatcher hands args to run() (with or without the command name), which the help tests (they stop before run) and ruff do not see.

After the move, in the same change: delete the moved commands from bin/relay's docstring, COMMANDS and imports (same commit as the new modules; commit A is "moved verbatim", reviewed with `git diff -M --color-moved=zebra`); (this is move 10: the guard's table is deleted here, see above); rewrite the `where` of open queue items that name the moved commands in bin/relay to the new module files, and record how many items the start filter holds before and after.

Start rule: the move takes named top-level functions and constants out of bin/relay. It starts when no running lane has changed anything it takes: read a lane's change with `git diff -U0 master...<lane> -- bin/relay` and compare each hunk's line range on master with the spans of the taken names (a hunk inside another function does not block). The item names bin/relay, so the start filter refuses it; start it with `relay queue start --despite-wait` when this rule says it is free. If a lane holding a taken function has not landed within 60 minutes, start anyway and that lane ports its hunk. Before landing, read again: the move lands whatever the second read shows; a lane that changed a moved function ports its hunk when it takes the default branch (git shows a conflict in the deleted function; the fixer reapplies the hunk to the new module); the landing note names the lane, the function and the new file.

Traps for this move: keep imports lint-clean (ruff F; a dropped import of a helper is ruff F821); tests that import from the repo root must still run under the short gate; done items name their `test` ids, which are found by name, so do not rename tests; RULE_TESTS names in lib/relay_textonly.py must stay valid; tests never touch the live .relay/queue (use a temporary folder); a move that takes a function another running lane changed ports that lane's hunk by hand (start rule below); the size marker leaves a file in the move that brings it under 600 lines.
why: Move 10 of the split of relay into one module per subcommand. The owner decided it on 28 Oct: "каждая подкоманда может и должна жить в своем модуле, этот подход должен быть распространен на весь relay". Waits for move 9 (changed, gate, precheck, check) and move 5 (the guard reads modules). bin/relay ends at about 15 lines and the shared-file pairs through bin/relay reach 0. This move edits plugins/delegate/hooks/read-only-guard.py (a paid-path change).
